title: DOISST steps make 2001-2022 annual-regression feedback more negative in five linear models
abstract: We tested how the feedback estimator changes the effect of fixed published SST step corrections. We used verified annual SST and radiation response series from five atmosphere-model Green's functions. For 2001-2022, raw-minus-corrected DOISST feedback is -0.132 and -0.103 W m-2 K-1 in annual regression for the in situ and CCI correction fits. The trend-ratio effects are -0.037 and +0.031. Annual-regression effects are negative in all five models; trend-ratio effects have both signs. An exact covariance identity shows that the change in the share of SST variance explained by time accounts for 76% and 125% of the net regression differences. All 15 tested one-to-five-year averaging phases keep the recent mean regression effects negative. Conditional block intervals for DOISST include zero. OI v2's June 2018 correction has a negative effect with both estimators, but the regression effect is 62% smaller. The long window, 1982-2022, gives different DOISST signs. These fixed-record results show that an artifact estimate must use the target feedback estimator. They do not validate the corrections, measure observed radiation, or constrain climate sensitivity. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and retrieval instructions are included.
